name: Facet
text: Adopt a dark theme by default with a one-click toggle to light mode. This keeps the interface consistently readable in low light while giving users control—matching competitors like Manus and Graphify. Trade-off: dark themes can strain readability for some users, but the toggle mitigates this.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes don’t solve the core problem: users who need light mode for readability will still toggle it on, but the toggle itself adds cognitive load—every time they open the tool, they must decide. A better alternative is default light mode with a persistent, high-contrast dark mode toggle, which reduces friction for the majority while still offering the option. Settle it by testing both with users who report readability issues—measure how often they toggle and whether their task completion speed improves.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Persistent high-contrast dark mode still forces a binary choice—users either adapt to the default or fight it every session. The real risk is that neither group gets the *adaptive* experience they need: light-mode readers get no dynamic relief, dark-mode users still toggle manually. Settle this with A/B testing: measure readability speed and preference in both defaults, not just toggle counts.
